stages.report:
FALSIFIED
The belief did not beat its pre-registered benchmark on past data, so the past record does not support shorting BTC for two days after a >5% daily drop.

**What was tested**
The rule is: If BTC/USDT closes down more than 5% in a day, open a short at the next day's open and close at the end of the second holding day. Data from 2017-08-17 to 2026-10-29. Completed trades 169 from 184 signals, average bars held 2.0, time in the market 10.06%.

**Strongest evidence against**
Random-entry baseline failed. Rule mean -0.35% vs random-entry mean -0.49%; the rule beat 64% of 2000 random sets, one-sided p = 0.357. The pass criterion required p below 0.05. Fee and slippage sensitivity failed: at 0.25% per side the mean trade is -0.65%. The rule does not hold in both halves: -0.42% (n=124) then -0.16% (n=45). It does not travel: better than random on only 0 of 9 other assets.

**What held up**
Sample size passed with 169 completed trades from 184 signals. Look-ahead guard passed; conditions use only past and current bars and every trade opens at the next bar's open. Nearby parameters passed; 6 of 6 nearby variants point the same way with median -0.40%.

**What would change the verdict**
A one-sided p below 0.05 versus random entries with the same holding period, with at least 20 trades, and robustness to fees, time splits and other assets.

**Caveats**
Rule compounded -60.3% while just holding the asset over the same window returned 1720.08%. Average net return per trade -0.35%, median -0.2%, share of winning trades 47.34%, worst drawdown -77.99%.
